n: This April 26, 1838, revelation at Far West is addressed first to the First Presidency—Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Hyrum Smith—and their counselors.

f.w: your counselors who are and shall be appointed hereafter
f.g: Assistant counselors were also appointed to the First Presidency in this period.

n: It is also addressed to Edward Partridge, the bishop in Missouri, and his counselors.
And to the high council in Zion and all members worldwide. The Lord now gives his Church its formal name.

f.w: scattered abroad in all the world

n: The Church’s name is revealed: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It puts Christ at the center and identifies members as “saints”—believers—in the last days.

f.w: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

f.g: “Saint” in the New Testament means a member of the community of believers, not a perfect person. Earlier names included “Church of Christ” and “Church of the Latter Day Saints.”

n: Echoing Isaiah, the Saints are called to rise and let their light become a banner other nations can see and follow.

f.g: A flag or banner raised as a rallying point.

n: Gathering to Zion and its stakes offers protection and refuge from spiritual and physical storms in the last days.
Far West is declared holy ground—language recalling God’s words to Moses at the burning bush.

f.w: the ground upon which thou standest is holy

n: The Saints are commanded to build a temple in Far West as a gathering place for worship.
Preparatory work and a foundation are to begin that summer.

f.g: Cornerstones for the Far West Temple were laid July 4, 1838.

n: The work is to begin on July 4, 1838—a date chosen with patriotic significance—and continue diligently.

f.w: the fourth day of July next
f.g: The cornerstones were laid on Independence Day 1838, as commanded.

n: Exactly one year later they are to recommence laying the foundation. Though mobs drove the Saints out that winter, apostles secretly returned on April 26, 1839, to fulfill this command.

f.w: in one year from this day

n: Once begun, the work should continue until the temple is entirely finished, top to bottom.

f.g: The foundation stone at a building’s corner, laid first.

n: Debt had nearly crushed the Church after Kirtland. The Lord instructs the First Presidency not to go into debt again to build a temple.
The temple must follow a pattern the Lord himself will reveal—as with Moses’ tabernacle and the Kirtland Temple.
If the Saints don’t follow the revealed pattern, the Lord will not accept the building.
If they do follow it, as shown through Joseph and his counselors, the Lord will accept it from his people.
Far West should be built up quickly as Saints gather there.

f.g: Far West grew rapidly in 1838, reaching an estimated several thousand people before the Saints were expelled that winter.

n: Other nearby places would become stakes as Joseph received direction, such as Adam-ondi-Ahman.

f.w: other places should be appointed for stakes

n: The Lord stands behind Joseph and has given him the keys of the kingdom and ministry.
